name: Industrial Dust Extractor
definition: A commercial or industrial vacuum system documented to capture task-generated dust at a tool, shroud or cleanup attachment through a hose, collection container, filter system and vacuum motor.
includedScope: Wet-and-dry extractors with documented task and dust boundaries
excludedScope: Combustible or explosive dust without exact approval
Asbestos or other hazardous dust without the required machine class and controls
primaryApplications: Construction cleanup within approved dust limits
headline: Industrial dust extractor classes, airflow, filtration and buyer verification
description: This technical profile separates tool-connected dust extraction from ordinary vacuuming and explains dust class, airflow, filter cleaning, collection and disposal boundaries.
metaDescription: Industrial dust extractor guide covering dust class, filters, airflow, tool connection, representative models and procurement checks.
disclaimer: This is an independent category reference, not exposure-control, combustible-dust, asbestos, electrical-safety or certification advice. Classify the actual dust and atmosphere, then verify the exact regional machine, filter, bag, hose, tool and work-practice approval.

keyFacts.label: System boundary
keyFacts.value: Tool shroud, hose, inlet, collection, filters, motor, monitoring and exhaust
keyFacts.evidence: Official manuals and product pages describe these linked subsystems on reviewed extractors.
keyFacts.scope: Functional synthesis; layouts and controls differ by model.

keyFacts.label: Dust-class boundary
keyFacts.value: A class label applies only to the exact machine and configuration
keyFacts.evidence: Reviewed manufacturers identify M-class models and IEC 60335-2-69 defines the commercial vacuum and extractor safety scope.
keyFacts.scope: Regional certification, filter and dust remain configuration-specific.

keyFacts.label: Task-control boundary
keyFacts.value: The extractor must match the tool manufacturer's required airflow and control method
keyFacts.evidence: OSHA Table 1 requires specified dust-collection characteristics for named United States construction silica tasks.
keyFacts.scope: 29 CFR 1926.1153 construction tasks in the United States only.

keyFacts.label: Disposal boundary
keyFacts.value: Filter cleaning and dust disposal can re-expose the operator
keyFacts.evidence: OSHA guidance and manufacturer documents identify controlled filter cleaning, bags and disposal procedures.
keyFacts.scope: Actual dust, work practice and jurisdiction.

systemFlow.name: Source capture
systemFlow.role: Intercepts dust near the generation point.
systemFlow.evidence: Official sources document tool connection and task-specific pickup.

systemFlow.name: Transport
systemFlow.role: Carries contaminated air to the extractor.
systemFlow.evidence: Reviewed machines use defined hose and adapter systems.
systemFlow.scope: Diameter, length, conductivity and seals are model-specific.

systemFlow.name: Primary collection
systemFlow.role: Retains bulk material and supports controlled disposal.
systemFlow.evidence: Manufacturer sources publish containers and approved bag systems.
systemFlow.scope: Usable capacity and bag type depend on material and configuration.

systemFlow.name: Filtration and cleaning
systemFlow.role: Limits dust passing to the exhaust and restores airflow according to design.
systemFlow.evidence: Official sources document filter classes, filter cleaning and monitoring on named models.
systemFlow.scope: Exact filter code, condition and cleaning setting.

systemFlow.name: Airflow generation and warning
systemFlow.role: Creates airflow and may alert the operator when flow falls below the configured threshold.
systemFlow.evidence: Reviewed product pages publish turbine data or airflow monitoring features.
systemFlow.scope: Source measurement point and alarm setup differ.

variants.name: Mains M-class extractor
variants.taskScale: Continuous tool-connected construction and workshop tasks
variants.operatorRelationship: Extractor follows the operator or remains beside the work zone
variants.spaceConstraints: Cable, hose routing and container footprint require control
variants.limitations: M-class naming does not approve combustible dust or every silica task.
variants.evidence: Festool, Bosch, Metabo and Milwaukee publish mains M-class models.

variants.name: Wet-and-dry construction extractor
variants.taskScale: Mixed approved dry dust and liquid pickup
variants.operatorRelationship: Requires mode, bag and filter changes according to instructions
variants.spaceConstraints: Wet pickup changes bag and filter handling
variants.limitations: Wet-and-dry capability does not permit all liquids or dusts.
variants.evidence: Official sources document wet-and-dry use for named models.

variants.name: Automatic-filter-cleaning extractor
variants.taskScale: High dust-loading tasks where the approved filter-cleaning system supports airflow
variants.operatorRelationship: Operator must configure and maintain the cleaning system
variants.spaceConstraints: Pulse noise and dust handling remain site considerations
variants.limitations: Automatic cleaning does not prove constant pickup or eliminate filter service.
variants.evidence: Festool, Bosch, Metabo and Milwaukee describe automatic filter cleaning.

performanceMetrics.name: Airflow
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Supports matching extractor flow to the connected tool requirement
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Turbine, hose-end and loaded-system values are not equivalent
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Compare only matched methods, hose and filter states.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Manufacturers and OSHA identify airflow as a task-control parameter.

performanceMetrics.name: Vacuum pressure
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Often reported at the turbine under source-defined conditions
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: High vacuum alone does not establish capture at the tool.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official product data publishes vacuum values for selected models.

performanceMetrics.name: Dust class and filter efficiency
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Defines part of the approved dust-control configuration
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Class, filter grade and whole-machine leakage are distinct
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Do not substitute a filter label for machine certification.
performanceMetrics.evidence: IEC and product pages distinguish commercial safety and M-class models.

performanceMetrics.name: Container and bag capacity
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Supports route, disposal and consumable planning
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Gross container and usable bag capacities differ
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Capacity does not establish safe fill level for the dust.

performanceMetrics.name: Tool socket and electrical load
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Supports automatic start and connected-tool planning
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Permitted connected load varies with voltage and market
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Do not use a catalogue maximum without the regional manual.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official sources document sockets or automatic tool activation on named models.

applicationFit.evidence: Manufacturers and OSHA document source-capture systems for named construction tasks.
applicationFit.scope: Exact tool, shroud, hose, extractor and United States Table 1 task where applicable.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Selection should start with the exposure-control plan and tool requirement, not extractor tank size.
applicationFit.limitations: No universal silica compliance is established.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Obtain the tool manufacturer's required airflow and written approval for the complete system.

applicationFit.evidence: Reviewed manufacturers position named M-class extractors for wood or renovation dust under stated limits.
applicationFit.scope: Named products; dust identity and limits remain site-specific.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Antistatic routing, bag choice and filter-cleaning behavior require an actual tool trial.
applicationFit.basis: Official system features and material examples.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Classify the dust and atmosphere, then trial the exact hose, tool and disposal setup.

applicationFit.evidence: Official sources include floor tools and wet/dry cleanup within model instructions.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: A tool-connected extractor may clean floors, but accessory handling and bag cost can differ from a facility vacuum.
applicationFit.basis: Reviewed supplied tools and collection architecture.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Run a cleanup trial and record pickup, blockages, filter events and disposal time.

applicationFit.application: Combustible, explosive or specially regulated dust
applicationFit.evidence: IEC safety scope and manufacturer warnings require product-specific approval and exclude unsupported atmospheres.
applicationFit.scope: Actual material, concentration, zoning and jurisdiction.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: A conventional M-class extractor should not be assumed suitable.
applicationFit.limitations: This profile provides no hazardous-location approval.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Stop selection until a competent assessment identifies the required certified system and work practice.

componentStack.name: Tool shrouds and adapters
componentStack.role: Capture dust at generation and connect the tool to the hose.
componentStack.evidence: OSHA and manufacturers require task-specific source capture.

componentStack.name: Hose and conductive path
componentStack.role: Transport dust while controlling leakage and static according to design.
componentStack.evidence: Official sources document model-specific hose systems.

componentStack.name: Collection and disposal system
componentStack.role: Retain material and permit controlled removal.
componentStack.evidence: Manufacturer manuals and OSHA guidance distinguish bags and handling.

componentStack.name: Filter and cleaning mechanism
componentStack.role: Limit exhaust dust and restore flow according to the design.
componentStack.evidence: Reviewed sources publish named filter and cleaning systems.

componentStack.name: Turbine, controls and alarms
componentStack.role: Generate airflow, start with tools and warn of restricted flow where fitted.
componentStack.evidence: Official pages document model-specific controls and monitoring.

representativeModels.evidence: Festool publishes the named model and technical data.
representativeModels.scope: Illustrations and delivered variants can differ by country.

representativeModels.evidence: Hilti's current manual identifies VC 40M-X and its M-class boundary.
representativeModels.scope: Exact regional product and accessories must be confirmed.

representativeModels.evidence: Makita publishes the model as a professional M-class dust extractor.
representativeModels.scope: UK configuration; verify local product number.

representativeModels.evidence: Metabo's official catalogue identifies the named model and features.
Bosch publishes the exact regional model and cited data.
Milwaukee publishes the model, features and technical values.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Complete tool-shroud-hose-extractor system and required airflow
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Buying by dust class or motor watts alone
procurementDecisions.evidence: OSHA specifies task controls and manufacturer airflow requirements for covered tasks.
procurementDecisions.scope: Exact United States construction task or relevant local rule.
procurementDecisions.assessment: The compliance evidence should name every system element.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Request written system approval and run an exposure-control verification where required.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Measure or verify loaded airflow with the delivered hose, filter and tool.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Filter cleaning, alarm behavior and sustained loaded airflow
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Treating maximum turbine airflow as achieved tool flow
procurementDecisions.evidence: Manufacturers publish automatic cleaning and monitoring on named models.
procurementDecisions.scope: Exact filter, hose and operating mode.
procurementDecisions.assessment: A dust-loading trial should record alarms, cleaning events and tool capture.
procurementDecisions.limitations: Catalogue maxima are not sustained-system results.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Run the intended tool and material through a representative duty cycle.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Confirm alarm threshold, filter-cleaning setting and hose diameter.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Bag, closure, filter-change and waste route
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Comparing gross tank litres as usable hazardous-dust capacity
procurementDecisions.evidence: Manufacturer and OSHA guidance emphasize controlled handling.
procurementDecisions.assessment: Consumables and change procedure belong in the purchase specification.
procurementDecisions.basis: Re-exposure risk during maintenance and disposal.
procurementDecisions.limitations: Waste classification is site- and jurisdiction-specific.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Approve a documented bag and filter change procedure before deployment.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Verify closure, storage, replacement stock and service access.

engineeringChecks.reason: Machine class cannot be selected without knowing material and ignition or health hazards.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Obtain a competent assessment before model selection.
engineeringChecks.evidence: IEC and OSHA requirements are hazard- and task-specific.

engineeringChecks.reason: Hose, filter loading and tool geometry reduce capture from turbine maxima.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Verify the complete system against the tool requirement.
engineeringChecks.evidence: OSHA and manufacturer sources make airflow and filter condition part of control.

engineeringChecks.reason: Incorrect consumables can change containment and service procedure.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: List exact approved part numbers and change methods in acceptance documents.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Official manuals distinguish filters and bags by application.

engineeringChecks.reason: Voltage and allowed connected load vary by region.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Confirm the regional rating plate, plug and tool load.

standards.name: IEC 60335-2-69:2021
standards.applicability: Safety of commercial wet, dry and wet-and-dry vacuum cleaners and dust extractors, including attachment-equipped machines.
standards.scope: Confirm local adoption and exact product conformity.

standards.name: OSHA 29 CFR 1926.1153
standards.applicability: Respirable crystalline silica exposure controls, including specified dust-collection requirements for named construction tasks.
standards.evidence: OSHA publishes Table 1 and alternative exposure-control requirements.
standards.scope: Covered United States construction work only; not a machine certification.

developments.title: IEC commercial vacuum and extractor safety edition published
developments.evidence: The IEC catalogue records the publication date and scope.
developments.scope: International base standard; local adoption differs.

developments.title: OSHA clarified filter and silica-waste handling
developments.summary: OSHA explained that handling contaminated filters and dust should minimize worker exposure and cited sealed disposal and HEPA-filtered cleaning examples.
developments.scope: United States silica standards and facts presented in the letter.
